topic: a PostgreSQL-style query workload on SQLite whose report is wrong because of NULL handling and a timezone bug across several SQL views
calibration:
Calibration: recent tasks and how often the reference agent solved them (target: 1-3 of 5 runs).
- fix-c-makefile-lib-reorg [medium]: 5/5 -> too_easy. Fix a C project's Makefile after a library reorganization broke include paths and linker flags
- fix-sqlite-migration-corruption [medium]: 5/5 -> too_easy. Diagnose and repair a SQLite database where a migration script silently shuffled data into wrong columns during a table recreation.
- nginx-proxy-swapped-routes [medium]: 5/5 -> too_easy. Fix an nginx reverse proxy that routes requests to the wrong backend services due to swapped upstream ports and missing path-stripping slashes.
- pillow-10-resampling-migration [medium]: 5/5 -> too_easy. Fix a thumbnail library whose test suite broke after a Pillow 10.x dependency upgrade removed Image.ANTIALIAS.
- cmake-visibility-plugin-crash [hard]: 5/5 -> too_easy. Diagnose and fix a CMake C++ project whose shared library hides symbols needed by dynamically loaded plugins, causing runtime symbol-resolution failures
Design this task harder than the too_easy ones and easier than the too_hard ones.

problems: at least one fault must be hidden by another (set `depends_on`), so fixing one reveals the next

too_easy_because: instruction.md names /app/queries/ directly, eliminating any need to trace the report generation pipeline
instruction.md names 'Newfoundland (NA-NFL)' specifically, immediately pointing the agent to the affected region and its data

instruction.md spells out the correct behavior for each fault ('count every shipment regardless of status', 'compute average weight as the mean of non-NULL weights only'), essentially describing the fix
instruction.md mentions /app/config.json under reference_regions as the timezone source of truth, removing the discovery step
The avg weight formula (SUM/COUNT(*) vs AVG) is in a single file and is a well-known SQL antipattern — trivially spotted on reading
Only 8 SQL files exist — agent can cat them all in one command; no real search required
Only 2 layers (code + data) with no build/config layer fault; no fault that blocks or hides another in practice
The chaining (fault 2 depends on fault 1) is negated because the instruction describes both symptoms explicitly — the agent can find both independently by reading files
No mechanism prevents the agent's fixes from taking effect; rebuild_views.sh just works
The WHERE clause is in a file called 'filtered_events' — the name itself signals the filtering behavior
